findings.title: Date overrides bypass busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before the subsequent `busy.every` check. Existing bookings and calendar events are still reported in `busy`, so a host can be shown as available during an override despite already being booked, allowing a double booking. An override should replace regular working hours, not ignore busy times.

findings.title: Multiple override windows reject each other
findings.body: The `.find` callback returns a truthy value when the slot is outside the current override window, which immediately marks the slot unavailable without checking later windows. For example, with overrides 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a slot in either window is rejected because it falls outside the other one. Check whether the slot fits any window for that date instead.

findings.title: Slots only need to overlap an override to be accepted
findings.body: These checks reject slots wholly before or after an override, but accept any slot that overlaps it. For example, a 09:30–10:30 slot passes a 10:00–11:00 override even though it starts outside the host's availability. This can incorrectly count a fixed host as available for a slot generated from another host; require the entire slot to fit within the override.

findings.title: Split working-hour windows make slots unavailable
findings.body: This rejects a slot if `.find` finds any working-hour interval that does not contain it, rather than rejecting only when no interval contains it. With 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 hours, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the second interval. Hosts with multiple windows on a day can therefore lose their availability.

findings.title: Working-hour check ignores the event end time
findings.body: `end` is calculated identically to `start`, so the check only verifies that the slot begins within a working-hour interval. A fixed host whose hours end at 10:00 can consequently be treated as available for a 09:30 slot lasting 60 minutes, even though the event ends at 10:30. Check the slot's actual end against the interval end.

findings.title: Timezone conversion drops date changes across midnight
findings.body: The timezone adjustment can move an override to the previous or next day, but this code keeps only its hour and minute and later anchors those to the unshifted invitee day. The active-override filter also selects overrides using the unshifted start date. For example, an override at 00:30 in UTC+5:30 maps to 19:00 on the prior UTC day, but is selected and placed on the original date for a UTC invitee. Availability near timezone day boundaries is therefore missing or shown on the wrong day.

findings.title: Timezone test can pass when expected slots are missing
findings.body: This assertion uses `toHaveTimeSlots`, whose implementation iterates the actual slots and compares each with the expected slot at that index. If the result contains only a matching prefix—for example, one of the four expected slots—the matcher still passes. The new timezone regression test therefore does not ensure that all expected slots are returned.
